Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9538 at 10 FR 4057, in the Federal Register of April 17, 1945 (govinfo file FR-1945-04-17, PDF page 1; text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The masthead date line in the OCR text layer is garbled and is not used. The order is headed Executive Order 9538, is signed April 13, 1945, and its filing line reads Filed, Apr. 14, 1945. Text and inventory: one operative paragraph, confirmed as one clause. Under section 1753 of the Revised Statutes and section 2 of the Civil Service Act, it authorizes the Civil Service Commission to certify for probational appointment any person whose name was on a list of eligibles between May 1, 1940 and March 16, 1942 (for the field service of the Post Office Department, October 23, 1943), who entered the armed forces between those dates and was honorably separated and remains qualified, who stood higher on the list than another applicant who received a probational appointment, and who asks for restoration or certification within ninety days after the end of military service or of hospitalization continuing after discharge for not more than one year, or within ninety days after the date of the order, whichever is later. A proviso excludes cases in which the list had expired before the applicant entered the armed forces and the Commission had not sustained objections to his certification because of his draft status. Ending: Executive Order 9733, signed June 4, 1946 and printed at 11 FR 6127 in the Federal Register of June 6, 1946 (held govinfo text layer), states in paragraph 3 that it supersedes Executive Order "No. 9538 of April 13, 1945", naming it also by title. Its paragraph 1 authorizes and directs the Commission to certify the same four classes on the same conditions and proviso, and paragraph 2 adds further classes. Executive Order 9733 has no effective-date wording, so the end is dated on signing, 1946-06-04; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the filing date (June 4, 1946) and publication date (June 6, 1946) are not used. Later event: Part III of Executive Order 9830, signed February 24, 1947 and printed at 12 FR 1259, lists "No. 9538 of April 13, 1945." among the orders revoked; its enacting clause reads "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:". That revocation fell on an order already superseded and is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. Executive Order 9598 of August 17, 1945 states that it "does not supersede or modify Executive Order No. 9538 of April 13, 1945", so it is a recital that leaves the order unchanged and is disclosed in a source note. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 9733 supersession, the Executive Order 9830 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 9598. The held-text number search found this number in the texts of Executive Orders 9598 and 9733, in Federal Register text files of the order's own issue and of the Executive Order 9598 issue, and in a Civil Service Commission cross-reference printed with Executive Order 9733.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10103 at 15 FR 597, in the Federal Register of February 3, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads 597 with the date Friday, February 3, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10103, Amendment of Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to Certain Public International Organizations, and is signed February 1, 1950. The held page also prints neighbouring documents, which are outside the inventory. Text and inventory: an enacting paragraph amending Executive Order 9721 and two numbered amendments, recorded as three clauses. Amendment 1 adds to section 1 of Executive Order 9721, effective as of May 10, 1946, a sentence beginning "Any employee so transferred shall, for a period not to exceed three years from the date of transfer", which treats a transferred employee as on leave of absence from federal employment while employed by the organization, provided he is later reemployed under section 3. Amendment 2 revives section 2 of Executive Order 9721, which had become inoperative on May 10, 1949, effective as of that date, and restates it: it gives competitive status to certain transferred war-service indefinite employees, and treats employees serving in an organization on September 30, 1949 as in active-duty status on that date for the purposes of Executive Order No. 10080. Partial revocation in 1959: section 2 of Executive Order 10804, signed February 12, 1959 and printed at 24 FR 1147 in the Federal Register of February 14, 1959 (held govinfo text layer), lists Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, Executive Order No. 10103 of February 1, 1950, and Executive Order No. 10774 of July 25, 1958, the last "insofar as it affects any employee covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic" Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957; the singular qualifier attaches to Executive Order 10774 alone. All three are revoked, except that "each shall be considered to remain in effect with respect to any" employee subject to it who was serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and does not elect coverage under section 6 of that Act, and "for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order prior to the date of the enactment of the" Act. Executive Order 10103 was therefore revoked generally in 1959 but remained in effect for those two saved classes. Later presidential orders applied it as still in effect for saved employees: Executive Order 11138, signed January 7, 1964 (29 FR 225), and Executive Order 11303 (31 FR 11963, filed September 12, 1966) each modify Executive Order 9721 as amended by Executive Order 10103 by waiving the section 1 leave-of-absence limit for one named employee. The editorial note under 22 U.S.C. 288 found by the machine U.S. Code search likewise records that the orders were revoked with certain savings provisions by section 2 of Executive Order 10804 and subsequently revoked by Executive Order 12553. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10103 with the subject "Amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. The table also lists 9721. That revocation, without exception, is the first end of the saved remainder and so of the whole order. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the 1959 revocation in part by Executive Order 10804, the Executive Order 11138 and 11303 modifications, the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference to Executive Order 10080. The held-text number search found this number in the texts of Executive Orders 10804, 11138 and 11303, in Federal Register text files of the order's own issue, and in a Civil Service Commission regulation's authority citation.

The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The report date of September 4, 1951 is a deadline, not an end. The order keeps the Board in existence until the President terminates it, but no held source records such a termination, so that contingency supplies no earlier end. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10283 at 16 FR 8873, in the Federal Register of September 1, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10283 and is signed August 30, 1951. Text: the order recites certain labor disputes between Kennecott Copper Corporation, Phelps Dodge Corporation, American Smelting and Refining Company, Anaconda Copper Mining Company (including International Smelting and Refining Company) and other employers engaged in mining, milling, smelting or refining copper or other non-ferrous metals, and certain of their employees represented by labor organizations including the International Union of Mine, Mill and Smelter Workers, several Railroad Brotherhoods and unions affiliated with the American Federation of Labor, and recites the President's opinion that strikes or lockouts in the industry would imperil the national health and safety. Invoking section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, it creates a Board of Inquiry, with members to be appointed by the President, to inquire into the issues involved in those disputes. It provides that "The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act", that the Board shall report to the President under section 206 "on or before September fourth, 1951", and that upon submitting its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as the Act requires, "until the Board is terminated by the President." Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the sentence on the Board's continued existence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10283 with a subject line describing a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the copper and nonferrous metals industry (the text layer misreads one letter of that row, so it is paraphrased here). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the Federal Register text file of the order's own printing.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10285 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain workers and a railroad operated by the Secretary of the Army. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline is not an end; the board reported on September 19, 1951 (held report), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.
